what.quote: A violently rotating column of air, usually pendant to a cumulonimbus, with circulation reaching the ground. It nearly always starts as a funnel cloud and may be accompanied by a loud roaring noise. On a local scale, it is the most destructive of all atmospheric phenomena.

what.quote: A warm-core, non-frontal synoptic-scale cyclone, originating over tropical or subtropical waters with organized deep convection and a closed surface wind circulation about a well-defined center.

nws-glossary-tornado.licence: US Government work, no copyright in the US.

row.definition: A violently rotating column of air, usually pendant to a cumulonimbus, with circulation reaching the ground. It nearly always starts as a funnel cloud and may be accompanied by a loud roaring noise. On a local scale, it is the most destructive of all atmospheric phenomena.

nws-glossary-tornado.title: NWS glossary: Tornado

nws-glossary-tropical-cyclone.licence: US Government work, no copyright in the US.

row.definition: A warm-core, non-frontal synoptic-scale cyclone, originating over tropical or subtropical waters with organized deep convection and a closed surface wind circulation about a well-defined center.

nws-glossary-tropical-cyclone.title: NWS glossary: Tropical Cyclone

rule-recipe-tc.method: Box 1500 by 1500 km centred on the row with the highest wind; a 12 km grid; start at the 00Z or 12Z cycle 24 hours before that row; 48 hours long; GFS for cycles from 2021-03-01 on, ERA5 before.
rule-recipe-tc.title: Seed recipe for a tropical cyclone

rule-recipe-tornado.method: A square box centred on the middle of the path, 600 km or the path's extent plus 300 km, whichever is larger; a 3 km grid; start at the 00Z, 06Z, 12Z or 18Z cycle at least 6 hours before the tornado; long enough to pass its end by 3 hours, at least 12 hours; GFS for cycles from 2021-03-01 on, ERA5 before.
rule-recipe-tornado.title: Seed recipe for a tornado

rule-select-tc.method: Storms of IBTrACS since 1980 picked one by one when the Weather Library was built, one or more from each basin. Rarity counts storms of the same basin whose highest wind is at least as high, peaking within a month of the same time of year.
rule-select-tc.title: How tropical cyclones are chosen for the Weather Library

rule-select-tornado.method: Rows of the SPC tornado table picked one by one when the Weather Library was built. Rarity counts tornadoes that start in the same state, in the same three-month season, rated at least as high.
rule-select-tornado.title: How tornadoes are chosen for the Weather Library
